newsitem.title: CANADA: Hogs rushed out of Manitoba Red River flood area.
newsitem.headline: Hogs rushed out of Manitoba Red River flood area.

text.p: Tens of thousands of hogs were being rushed out of Manitoba's Red River Valley flood areas on Wednesday.

"Dairy cattle are pretty much out already, there's about eight to 12 herds, and there's numerous broiler laying (chicken) flocks. There's quite a number of hog operations that are making their decisions today," Manitoba Agriculture Emergency Management Organization coordinator Gus Wruck said.
Hogs represent the largest livestock market in Manitoba.
This year's flood may cover twice the area hit in 1950 and 1979, when some 400 square miles (1,036 square km) between the U.S. border and Winnipeg were under water.
The valley could take weeks to drain, said Larry Whitney, Manitoba Natural Resources flood liaison engineer.

"We're moving dairy cattle, hogs, chickens and even emus. There's still more to move. We're matching producers up with feeder barns for pigs almost on a minute-to-minute basis right now," Manitoba Agriculture's Morris district agriculture representative Denis Schindler said.
Highway 75 remained open to commercial trucks only, but was likely to be closed before day's end, a Manitoba Highways and Transportation official said.
The province ordered all 1,500 residents of Morris, Manitoba and 15,500 other Red River Valley residents to evacuate their homes on Wednesday.
Morris is about 45 kms (28 miles) north of the U.S. border.
